questions.q: What is the stated purpose of RESA?
choices: To maximize commissions for licensees
To protect the public
To set property tax rates
To regulate mortgage lenders only
questions.explain: RESA protects the public by setting competency requirements, conduct standards, and appointing a regulator (BCFSA).

questions.q: Which body makes the Real Estate Services Rules?
choices: The Lieutenant Governor in Council
BCFSA
BCREA
Each local real estate board
questions.explain: Since the 2021 amendments, BCFSA makes the Rules. The Regulation is made by Cabinet (the Lieutenant Governor in Council).

questions.q: The 2016 amendments increased the maximum discipline penalty for individuals from $10,000 to what?
questions.explain: Maximum penalties rose 25 times, from $10,000 to $250,000 for individuals.

questions.q: Under RESA s.3, which combination requires a licence (unless exempt)?
choices: Any real estate advice given to anyone, whether paid or not
Real estate services, for another, for actual or expected pay
Buying or selling property for yourself as an investor
Owning more than one property at the same time
questions.explain: All three elements must be present: real estate services, for another, for pay or expected pay.

questions.q: Which of these is NOT one of the three kinds of real estate services under RESA?
choices: Trading services
Rental property management services
Strata management services
Mortgage brokering services
questions.explain: Real estate services are trading, rental property management and strata management. Mortgage brokering is regulated under separate legislation.

questions.q: Is negotiating a commercial lease for a tenant a "trade in real estate"?
choices: No; only sales are trades, so leasing needs no licence
Yes; trades include leasing and assigning leases
Only if the lease is for a term of more than 3 years
Only if the property is residential, not commercial
questions.explain: A trade in real estate includes purchase, sale, leasing and other acquisitions or dispositions, plus assignments of purchase, sale or lease contracts.

questions.q: Selling a time share interest on behalf of another person for a fee:
choices: Never needs a licence, since a time share isn't land
Needs a licence; RESA's real estate includes time shares
Needs a licence only if the buyer lives in BC
Is regulated only under securities law, not RESA
questions.explain: RESA defines real estate to include cooperative interests, shared interests in land and time share interests, even if they aren't interests in land.

questions.q: A licensee helps their sister buy a condo for free. Does RESA apply?
choices: No, because there's no remuneration involved at all
No, because services for family members are always exempt
Yes; RESA covers unpaid services, so use the brokerage
Only if the sister signs a written service agreement
questions.explain: "Once a licensee, always a licensee": RESA covers services for yourself, unpaid services and otherwise exempt services. Everything goes through the brokerage.
questions.ref: Lesson 4 · Once a licensee, always a licensee

questions.q: Why is it risky for a licensee to list their own property themselves?
choices: It's illegal for a licensee to list their own property
Own-interest deals aren't covered by the E&O Indemnity Plan
Brokerages aren't allowed to list a licensee's property
The licensee's licence automatically becomes inoperative
questions.explain: Own-interest deals are excluded from E&O coverage, and an unrepresented buyer may allege abuse of position. Better to have another licensee act.
questions.ref: Lesson 4 · Once a licensee, always a licensee

questions.q: A developer offers to pay a licensee directly for selling units. What does RESA s.7 say?
choices: It's fine as long as the payment is disclosed to buyers
Services only through the brokerage, paid only by it
It's fine for commercial projects but not residential ones
It's fine if the developer is a close family member
questions.explain: Managing brokers, associate brokers and representatives must provide services only for their brokerage and must not accept pay from anyone else.
questions.ref: Lesson 4 · Once a licensee, always a licensee

questions.q: Which is exempt from licensing under RESA itself (s.3)?
choices: A notary public preparing the transfer documents
An executor dealing with the estate's real estate
An auctioneer selling land at a public auction
An appraiser who values the property for a fee
questions.explain: RESA s.3 exempts court-authorized persons, insolvency officials, executors/administrators, trustees, trust companies and practising lawyers. Notaries, auctioneers and appraisers are exempt under the Regulation.

questions.q: An accountant is paid to help a client sell a small business. Do they need a licence?
choices: Yes; anyone paid to help sell a business needs a licence
No; the Regulation exempts accountants on business sales
Only if the business owns land or a building
Only if the accountant advertises the business for sale
questions.explain: The Regulation's trading services exemptions include accountants acting on the purchase and sale of a business.

questions.q: An unlicensed salaried employee of a developer sells the developer's strata units. What must they do?
choices: Nothing, as long as they're on the developer's payroll
Disclose in writing, separately and before any agreement
Get a temporary licence from BCFSA within 30 days
Have a licensee review and co-sign every contract
questions.explain: Developer employees are exempt only if they make this separate written disclosure before any agreement is entered into.

questions.q: A licensee who owns a strata lot wants to sit on strata council under Rules s.96. Which is a condition?
choices: They may be paid the usual strata management fee
They must have sole signing authority over strata funds
Disclose in writing, copy the MB, no sole signing, no pay
They must provide the services through their brokerage
questions.explain: Section 96 requires written disclosure to the strata (copied to the managing broker), no sole signing or spending authority, and no remuneration.

questions.q: Which task may an unlicensed assistant of a trading licensee perform?
choices: Host an open house
Show a property to a buyer
Witness signatures
Present an offer
questions.explain: Unlicensed assistants may witness signatures, place signs, do filing, take messages and draft documents for approval. They can't host, show, advise, present or negotiate offers, or talk to consumers about deals.

questions.q: Who may show rental properties to prospective tenants without a licence?
choices: Anyone, since showing a rental isn't a regulated service
An unlicensed assistant of a property management licensee
An unlicensed assistant of a trading services licensee
No one; only licensees may ever show any property
questions.explain: There's a specific allowance for unlicensed assistants of property management licensees to show rentals to prospective tenants.

questions.q: Which is the overarching fiduciary duty?
choices: Duty to get the highest possible price
Loyalty: act solely for the client
Duty to obey all instructions, lawful or not
Duty of fairness to the other party
questions.explain: Loyalty is the overarching duty. The others are avoiding conflicts, full disclosure, confidentiality and obeying lawful instructions.

questions.q: Who is the Superintendent of Real Estate?
choices: An elected official
The chief executive officer of BCFSA
The president of BCREA
The chair of the E&O Insurance Corporation
questions.explain: The Superintendent is BCFSA's CEO, appointed by its board, and delegates most powers to BCFSA staff.

questions.q: Where does the interest on a brokerage's general trust account go?
choices: The brokerage, as income
The licensee on the file
The Real Estate Foundation
BCFSA, to fund regulation
questions.explain: Interest on general trust accounts goes to REFBC, except client-requested separate accounts and accounts holding tenants' deposits.
questions.ref: Lesson 4 · Three bodies that protect the public

questions.q: What is the E&O Indemnity Plan's limit, and does it include defence costs?
choices: $1 million, excluding defence costs
$2 million, including defence costs
$2 million, excluding defence costs
$5 million, including defence costs
questions.explain: The limit is $2 million per licence, and defence costs come out of that limit.
questions.ref: Lesson 4 · Three bodies that protect the public

questions.q: A licensee and their brokerage are both found liable and damages are paid. What deductible applies?
choices: None, because the brokerage is insured
$2,000 in total, shared between them
$2,000 each, so $4,000 in total
$5,000 each, so $10,000 in total
questions.explain: Each insured licensee pays a $2,000 deductible when damages are paid.
questions.ref: Lesson 4 · Three bodies that protect the public

questions.q: A claim against a licensee is dismissed at trial after the insurer spent $80,000 defending it. What deductible does the licensee pay?
choices: $2,000, the standard deductible
$80,000, the full defence cost
None, due to first-dollar defence
$4,000, double the deductible
questions.explain: First-dollar defence means no deductible where only defence costs were incurred and nothing was paid to the claimant.
questions.ref: Lesson 4 · Three bodies that protect the public

questions.q: Which is covered by the E&O Indemnity Plan?
choices: A $10,000 BCFSA discipline penalty
A commission dispute with another brokerage
A negligent misstatement of square footage
A claim over the licensee's own property sale
questions.explain: The plan covers negligent errors and omissions in providing real estate services. Penalties, commission disputes and own-interest deals are excluded.
questions.ref: Lesson 4 · Three bodies that protect the public

questions.q: What does "claims made" coverage mean?
choices: Any claim arising from an act during the policy is covered whenever reported
The claim must be reported during the policy term to be covered
Only claims over $2 million are covered
Claims must be made in BC
questions.explain: Under claims-made coverage, a claim must be reported during the policy term. An occurrence policy would cover acts during the term whenever reported.
questions.ref: Lesson 4 · Three bodies that protect the public

questions.q: A licensee steals a client's deposit and disappears. What's the most the Special Compensation Fund will pay that client?
choices: $1 million
$2 million
questions.explain: The maximum is $200,000 per claimant and $1 million per brokerage. E&O excludes fraud, so the Compensation Fund is the relevant protection.
questions.ref: Lesson 4 · Three bodies that protect the public

questions.q: Which statement about realtor.ca is correct?
choices: It's the MLS® system that boards use for cooperation
It's CREA's ad site showing MLS® listings, not the MLS®
It's run by BCFSA to show licensed brokerages' listings
It's a site used only for commercial listings in Canada
questions.explain: realtor.ca is a public advertising site created by CREA. The MLS® is the cooperative system run by boards for members.

questions.q: Is membership in a local real estate board required to hold a licence?
choices: Yes, every licensee must join a local real estate board
No, but it's needed for the MLS® and REALTOR® mark
Only managing brokers must join a board
Only licensees working in Greater Vancouver must join
questions.explain: Board membership is voluntary for licensing purposes but required for MLS® access and the REALTOR® mark.

questions.q: With whom does a client's service agreement legally exist?
choices: The individual representative
The brokerage
The managing broker personally
BCFSA
questions.explain: All services are provided through the brokerage; contracts are between the client and the brokerage.

questions.q: A brokerage's managing broker is licensed for trading and rental property management. Can a licensee at that brokerage provide strata management?
choices: Yes, if the licensee personally holds a strata licence
No; the managing broker's category limits the brokerage
Yes, as long as it's done through a registered team
Only with BCFSA's written permission for each strata
questions.explain: A brokerage may only provide services permitted by its managing broker's licence category.

questions.q: The managing broker's licence is suspended. What happens to the representatives' licences at that brokerage?
choices: Nothing; their licences are separate from the managing broker's
The brokerage and all related licences become inoperative
They transfer automatically to the nearest other brokerage
They're cancelled permanently and must be reapplied for
questions.explain: If the managing broker's licence is inoperative, suspended or cancelled, the brokerage licence becomes inoperative, and so do the licences of everyone engaged there.
questions.ref: Lesson 4 · Getting and keeping your licence

questions.q: A representative learns a colleague in the same brokerage has been taking secret commissions. What must they do?
choices: Nothing, because it's not their file
Promptly notify their managing broker
Confront the colleague privately only
Wait until a client complains
questions.explain: Rules s.29 requires associate brokers and representatives to promptly report misconduct, including other licensees' in their brokerage, to their managing broker.

questions.q: Two licensees regularly act as designated agents for the same clients but don't advertise as a team. Must they register as a team?
choices: No; only advertising as a team triggers registration
Yes; regularly acting for the same clients triggers it
Only if they share commissions under a written agreement
Only if their managing broker decides to require it
questions.explain: Registration is required if licensees present as a single entity, are regularly designated agents of the same client, or regularly work like implied agents of the same party.

questions.q: Can one team member represent the seller while another represents the buyer in the same deal?
choices: Yes, if both clients consent in writing
No; the whole team is the designated agent
Yes, if they work from different branch offices
Only in commercial deals, with disclosure
questions.explain: Teams can't separate agency relationships. The team collectively is the agent, and all members' names go on the contracts.

questions.q: Which service may a registered real estate team provide?
choices: Trading services only
Rental property management
Strata management
All three
questions.explain: Teams may provide trading services only. Licensed members can provide rental or strata management only outside the team.

questions.q: What protection does a personal real estate corporation give the licensee from third-party liability?
choices: Full protection, the same as any other corporation
None; it doesn't shield the licensee from liability
Protection up to the $2 million E&O limit only
Protection only for commercial transactions
questions.explain: A PREC is mainly for tax planning. It doesn't shield the licensee from liability, and misconduct by the PREC is treated as the individual's.

questions.q: What is the minimum age to be licensed as an individual?
questions.explain: Individual applicants must be at least 19 years old.
questions.ref: Lesson 4 · Getting and keeping your licence

questions.q: How recent must a licence applicant's criminal record check be?
choices: Within 30 days
Within 90 days
Within 1 year
There's no time limit
questions.explain: The original criminal record check must be dated within 90 days of BCFSA receiving the application.
questions.ref: Lesson 4 · Getting and keeping your licence

questions.q: What experience does a first-time associate or managing broker applicant need?
choices: None, if they've passed the Broker's Licensing Course
2 years as a licensee in the 5 years before applying
5 years as a licensee in the past 10 years
At least 10 completed transactions as a representative
questions.explain: Two years of licensed experience in the previous five years, in BC or an equivalent jurisdiction (waivable in some cases).
questions.ref: Lesson 4 · Getting and keeping your licence

questions.q: After passing the licensing exam, what must a new trading services applicant complete?
choices: Nothing more; the licence is issued after the exam
An Applied Practice Course (Residential or Commercial)
The Broker's Licensing Course and a broker's exam
A two-year apprenticeship with a managing broker
questions.explain: New trading licensees must complete one of BCFSA's Applied Practice Courses (about five months). A temporary licence is issued early in the course.
questions.ref: Lesson 4 · Getting and keeping your licence

questions.q: How long is a licence term, and when must you apply to renew?
choices: 1 year; apply 10 days before expiry
2 years; apply 30+ days before expiry
3 years; apply 60 days before expiry
5 years; apply any time before expiry
questions.explain: Licences run for two years. Apply at least 30 days before expiry; the licence then continues until BCFSA decides.
questions.ref: Lesson 4 · Getting and keeping your licence

questions.q: A licensee is charged (not convicted) with a criminal offence. Must they tell BCFSA?
choices: No; only convictions need to be reported to BCFSA
Yes; charges must be reported promptly, in writing
Only if the charge relates to a real estate transaction
Only at renewal, on the licence renewal application
questions.explain: Charges must be reported too. A licensee who thought only convictions counted was reprimanded and ordered to pay $1,500.
questions.ref: Lesson 4 · Getting and keeping your licence

questions.q: A licensee works from a home office. Which is allowed?
choices: A sign outside saying "Real estate services"
Answering the home phone in the brokerage's name
Putting the home address on business cards
None of these; all three are prohibited
questions.explain: Rules s.37: no visible sign, don't answer the phone in the brokerage's name, and don't put the personal office address on ads or records.
questions.ref: Lesson 4 · Getting and keeping your licence
